units.note: Greek ends mid-sentence (ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην,); English marks with [...].

findings.quote: vying with one another for Hasdrubal’s favor
findings.problem: ἀντιφιλοδοξοῦντες πρὸς τὸν Ἀσδρούβαν: the elephant-masters were rivalling Hasdrubal (competing with him for credit), not competing with one another for his favor; the next clause (βουλόμενοι δι᾽ αὑτῶν ποιῆσαι τὸ προτέρημα) confirms they wanted the success to be their own rather than the commander's.

findings.quote: he immediately sent them out together with his own men. To deal with the Gauls he sent Hannibal
findings.problem: εὐθέως μετ᾽ αὐτῶν ἀπέστειλε πρὸς μὲν τοὺς Κελτοὺς Ἀννίβαν…: μετ᾽ αὐτῶν means Hannibal and Alexon were sent along with the loyal officers (αὐτῶν = the officers who accepted his words); there are no 'his own men' in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: he immediately sent them out, and along with them he sent to the Gauls Hannibal

units.note: Remainder of the sentence (the son of the Hannibal who died in Sardinia; Alexon to the other mercenaries) is accurate.

findings.problem: φίλος Ἀτάρβου πρῶτος: the name is Ἀτάρβας (Atarbas), not Adherbal (Ἀδέρβας), a different person.

units.note: Greek breaks off mid-word (τῶν Καρχηδο-); English completes the sentence as if whole. The sense is recoverable, so no fix proposed, but the seam should be marked.
